purpose: VibeVoice-ASR Q4_K_M decode: pass the o_proj decode GEMV a caller-owned bf16 scratch instead of allocating one per layer per token
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 256-bit LPDDR5X, 133 GB unified

protocol.weights: Q4_K_M backbone (168 Q4_K + 28 Q6_K layer tensors) via /tmp/vibevoice-asr-q4km.gguf; dense bf16 lane via microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF
protocol.change: q4_dense_gemv_f32_bf16w_f32_out already accepted an x_bf16_scratch buffer, but its caller in forward_layers never supplied one, so the wrapper called malloc(7168)/free once per layer (28 pairs per decoded token). The runner now allocates one 7168-byte bf16 scratch at construction and passes it. No arithmetic changes: the same f32_to_bf16 narrowing and the same pack8 GEMV run on the same values.
protocol.workload: 89-row prompt, batched prefill, then 40 decoded tokens per timed trial at context 89-129; 2 warmup runs per lane before timing
protocol.method: all lanes measured in one process with the same loop, fixture and prompt rows, rotating lane order every trial so host drift cannot favour a lane; the two Q4 lanes differ only in where the o_proj input scratch comes from

gates.arithmetic_identity: bit-identical: every decoded token's full logits vector is byte-identical between the two Q4 lanes (SHA-256 per token, 40 tokens, 6,082,560 logits, first mismatch none), and the same 40-token chain. The comparison is per token over raw logits bytes, not a sum, because a sum can match while individual elements differ. Negative control: the dense bf16 lane's per-token logits differ from the Q4 lane on 40/40 tokens, so the comparison is demonstrably sensitive.
gates.gpu_suite_q4: 16 passed, 1 xfailed (tests/test_gpu_vibevoice_qwen2_q4_runner.py), unchanged from before the change
gates.gpu_suite_bf16: 8 passed (tests/test_gpu_vibevoice_qwen2_runner.py); the shared forward_layers passes the kwarg only when the runner owns a scratch, so the dense lane is byte-for-byte unaffected

profile.why: the change is byte-exact on the affected surface (per-token logits identical), so it meets the strict arithmetic contract, which is stronger than production requires.
profile.not_claimed: this artifact is not a full production qualification. Production promotion additionally requires the calibrated mean/p95/p99/max KL envelope, top-1 by category/shape, same-schedule determinism, isolation, BF16-relative and task-quality gates per docs/EXECUTION-PROFILES.md section 6, which were not run for this artifact.

notes: The 28 malloc/free pairs per token cost 3.8-5.5 ms/token, far more than the 7 KiB copy would suggest. Why is not measured here: the plausible reading is that hipMalloc/hipFree interleaved in the per-layer loop stalls the launch pipeline rather than merely adding allocation work, but this artifact measures the A/B delta, not the mechanism.
Removing them also cuts variance: across four runs the persistent-scratch lane held 48.1-49.1 ms/token while the per-layer-malloc lane ranged 51.9-55.1 ms/token.

The previously recorded 48.1 ms/token (artifact 2026-09-14-gfx1151-vibevoice-q4-pack8-decode.json) was measured with the same per-layer malloc, in a session whose dense bf16 lane measured 72.2 vs 74.75 ms/token here. The recorded absolute rate is therefore not comparable to this session's per-layer-malloc lane, and this artifact does not claim an old-to-new absolute improvement; the claim is the in-process A/B delta and the matched same-process ratio.
Matched in one process this session, Q4_K_M decode is 1.55x the dense bf16 lane (48.24 vs 74.75 ms/token), against 1.39x for the same Q4 lane with per-layer malloc.
